# Fieldset

A titled group of related fields, such as an address, rendered as a `<fieldset>` named by its legend. `disabled` disables every native control and every `Field` inside it at once.

```tsx
import { Fieldset } from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/field/fieldset";
```

## Example

```tsx
<Fieldset legend="Shipping address" description="Where we send your order.">
  <Field label="Street" name="street"><FieldControl autoComplete="street-address" /></Field>
  <Field label="City" name="city"><FieldControl autoComplete="address-level2" /></Field>
</Fieldset>
```

## Usage

A group of checkboxes or radios that make one choice uses their group component, which takes the same `legend`.

## Use instead when

- Use `Field` instead for a single control.

## Props

Type: `FieldsetProps`.

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` | The fields and controls in the group. |
| `className` | `string` | Layout only: margins, width, grid placement (`mt-6`). Appearance classes warn in development. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | Supporting text under the legend, read after it through `aria-describedby`. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Disables every native control and every `Field` inside it, and fades the legend. |
| `hideLegend` | `boolean` | Hides the legend visually; screen readers still read it as the group's name. |
| `legend` (required) | `string` | What the group is, shown above it and read as the group's name. Required: a group of controls needs a name. To hide it visually, keep it and add `hideLegend`. |

## Don't use

These are not props. Passing one fails the type check with the fix in the error, and in development a console message names the fix.

- `label`: Not a prop. Groups take `legend`: `<Fieldset legend="Shipping address">`.

## `className` is for layout only

Pass margins, width and grid placement (`mt-4`, `w-full`, `col-span-2`). Your classes always win over Ouro UI's: Fieldset merges `className` last with `cn` (tailwind-merge), so a class that conflicts with its own replaces it.[^layout-classes]

Appearance comes from props, not classes. In development, a class that sets appearance logs one warning per component instance, naming the prop to use instead. A class sets appearance when, after its variants (`hover:`, `sm:`) and any `!` are removed, it starts with `bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `rounded-`, `shadow-`, `font-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-` or `stroke-`, or is `border`, `rounded`, `shadow` or `ring`, or has a `dark:` variant. Text wrapping, overflow and table layout classes (`text-wrap`, `text-ellipsis`, `border-collapse`) are layout and do not warn.

Alignment classes (`text-center`) warn too: set alignment on a parent element.
